cves: Nezha from 2.1.0 before 2.3.15 contains a host header injection vulnerability in mintTransferTool that builds fs.download_url and fs.upload_url transfer URLs from the unvalidated Host header. Attackers who control the Host header seen on a victim's MCP request can redirect file uploads or capture one-time download tokens and replay them to exfiltrate files.

Nezha from 1.7.0 before 2.3.15 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated members to enumerate other tenants' server IDs through differential responses. Attackers can sweep sequential IDs against getServerConfig and setServerConfig, distinguishing 'permission denied' from success payloads to map other users' servers.

Nezha from 1.8.0 before 2.3.13 contains a lock-order inversion in UpdateGroup and DeleteGroup that allows authenticated non-admin users to deadlock the alerting subsystem. Attackers can concurrently call the notification-group and batch-delete endpoints with oversized id lists to widen the race and close an ABBA cycle, permanently killing alert delivery until restart.
